cues.en: Accuracy isn't the only thing that matters with recommender systems.
cues.zh: 推薦系統重要的不只是準確程度。

cues.en: There are other things we can measure if they're important to us. For example, coverage.
cues.zh: 如果對我們重要，還可以衡量其他事情，例如覆蓋率。

cues.en: That's just the percentage of possible recommendations that your system is able to provide.
cues.zh: 它就是系統能提供的推薦，占所有可能推薦的百分比。

cues.en: Think about the MovieLens data set of movie ratings we're using in this course.
cues.zh: 想想本課程使用的 MovieLens 電影評分資料集。

cues.en: It contains ratings for several thousand movies, but there are plenty of movies in existence that it doesn't have ratings for.
cues.zh: 它包含數千部電影的評分，但還有很多實際存在的電影，沒有包含在裡面。

cues.en: If you were using this data to generate recommendations on, say, IMDb, then the coverage of this recommender system would be low, because IMDb has millions of movies in its catalog, not thousands.
cues.zh: 如果用這份資料為 IMDb 產生推薦，覆蓋率就會很低，因為 IMDb 的目錄有數百萬部電影，而不是數千部。

cues.en: It's worth noting that coverage can be at odds with accuracy.
cues.zh: 覆蓋率可能與準確程度衝突。

cues.en: If you enforce a higher quality threshhold on the recommendations you make, then you might improve your accuracy at the expense of coverage.
cues.zh: 如果提高推薦的品質門檻，可能改善準確程度，卻犧牲覆蓋率。

cues.en: Finding the balance of where exactly you're better off recommending nothing at all can be delicate.
cues.zh: 要找到何時寧可什麼都不推薦的平衡點，可能很微妙。

cues.en: Coverage can also be important to watch, because it gives you a sense of how quickly new items in your catalog will start to appear in recommendations.
cues.zh: 覆蓋率也值得注意，因為它能讓你了解，目錄中的新項目會多快開始出現在推薦裡。

cues.en: When a new book comes out on Amazon, it won't appear in recommendations until at least a few people buy it, therefore establishing patterns with the purchase of other items.
cues.zh: Amazon 上有新書出版時，至少要有幾個人購買，建立它與其他商品購買行為的模式，才會出現在推薦中。

cues.en: Until those patterns exist, that new book will reduce Amazon's coverage metric.
cues.zh: 在這些模式建立之前，新書會拉低 Amazon 的覆蓋率指標。

cues.en: Another metric is called diversity.
cues.zh: 另一個指標叫做多樣性。

cues.en: You can think of this as a measure of how broad a variety of items your recommender system is putting in front of people.
cues.zh: 可以把它視為，推薦系統呈現給使用者的項目種類，有多廣泛。

cues.en: An example of low diversity would be a recommender system that just recommends the next books in a series that you've started reading, but doesn't recommend books from
cues.zh: 低多樣性的例子是，你開始讀某個系列後，系統只推薦同系列的後續書籍，卻不推薦

cues.en: different authors, or movies related to what you've read.
cues.zh: 其他作者的書，或與閱讀內容相關的電影。

cues.en: This may seem like a subjective thing, but it is measurable.
cues.zh: 這看起來可能很主觀，但其實可以衡量。

cues.en: Many recommender systems start by computing some sort of similarity metric between items, so we can use these similarity scores to measure diversity.
cues.zh: 許多推薦系統一開始會計算某種項目間相似度，因此可以利用這些相似度分數衡量多樣性。

cues.en: If we look at the similarity scores of every possible pair in a list of top-N recommendations, we can average them to get a measure of how similar the recommended items in the list are to each other.
cues.zh: 查看 Top-N 推薦清單中所有可能項目配對的相似度，再取平均，就能衡量清單中的推薦彼此有多相似。

cues.en: We can call that measure S.
cues.zh: 可以將這個數值稱為 S。

cues.en: Diversity is basically the opposite of average similarity, so we subtract it from 1 to get a number associated with diversity.
cues.zh: 多樣性基本上與平均相似度相反，因此用一減去它，得到與多樣性相關的數字。

cues.en: It's important to realize that diversity, at least in the context of recommender systems, isn't always a good thing.
cues.zh: 必須了解，至少在推薦系統的情境中，多樣性不一定是好事。

cues.en: You can achieve very high diversity by just recommending completely random items.
cues.zh: 只要完全隨機推薦項目，就能達到非常高的多樣性。

cues.en: But those aren't good recommendations by any stretch of the imagination.
cues.zh: 但無論怎麼看，那都不算好的推薦。

cues.en: Unusually high diversity scores mean that you just have bad recommendations more often than not.
cues.zh: 異常高的多樣性分數，往往代表推薦品質很差。

cues.en: You always need to look at diversity alongside metrics that measure the quality of the recommendations as well.
cues.zh: 一定也要搭配衡量推薦品質的指標，一起檢視多樣性。

cues.en: Similarly, novelty sounds like a good thing, but often it isn't.
cues.zh: 同樣地，新穎性聽起來是好事，但往往不然。

cues.en: Novelty is a measure of how popular the items are that you're recommending.
cues.zh: 新穎性衡量的是，被推薦的項目有多熱門。

cues.en: And again, just recommending random stuff would yield very high novelty scores since the vast majority of items are not top sellers.
cues.zh: 同樣地，只要隨機推薦，就會得到非常高的新穎性分數，因為絕大部分項目都不是暢銷品。

cues.en: Although novelty is measurable, what to do with it is in many ways subjective.
cues.zh: 雖然新穎性可以衡量，但該如何運用它，在許多方面都很主觀。

cues.en: There's a concept of user trust in a recommender system.
cues.zh: 推薦系統有一個概念，叫做使用者信任。

cues.en: People want to see at least a few familiar items in their recommendations that make them say, "Yeah, that's a good recommendation for me.
cues.zh: 人們希望推薦裡至少有幾個熟悉的項目，讓他覺得：「對，這個推薦很適合我。

cues.en: This system seems good."
cues.zh: 這個系統好像不錯。」

cues.en: If you only recommend things people have never heard of, they may conclude that your system doesn't really know them them, and they may engage less with your recommendations as a result.
cues.zh: 如果只推薦人們從沒聽過的東西，他們可能認為系統不了解自己，因此更少與推薦互動。

cues.en: Also, popular items are usually popular for a reason.
cues.zh: 而且，熱門項目之所以熱門，通常有其原因。

cues.en: They're enjoyable by a large segment of the population, so you would expect them to be good recommendations for a large segment of the population who hasn't read or watched them yet.
cues.zh: 它們受到很多人的喜愛，因此也可預期，對尚未閱讀或觀看的許多人來說，會是好的推薦。

cues.en: If you're not recommending some popular items, you should probably question whether your recommender system is really working as it should.
cues.zh: 如果完全不推薦一些熱門項目，或許該懷疑推薦系統是否真的正常運作。

cues.en: This is an important point. You need to strike a balance between familiar, popular items and what we call serendipitous discovery of new items the user has never heard of before.
cues.zh: 這一點很重要。你需要在熟悉的熱門項目，以及意外發現從沒聽過的新項目之間，取得平衡。

cues.en: The familiar items establish trust with the user, and the new ones allow the user to discover entirely new things that they might love.
cues.zh: 熟悉的項目建立使用者信任，新項目則讓使用者發現可能喜愛的全新事物。

cues.en: Novelty is important, though, because the whole point of recommender systems is to surface items in what we call "the long tail."
cues.zh: 不過，新穎性確實很重要，因為推薦系統的目的，就是讓所謂「長尾」中的項目浮上檯面。

cues.en: Imagine this is a plot of the sales of items of every item in your catalog, sorted by sales.
cues.zh: 想像這是一張依銷量排序、呈現目錄中每個項目銷售量的圖。

cues.en: So the number of sales, or popularity, is on the Y axis, and all the products are along the X axis.
cues.zh: 因此 Y 軸是銷量或熱門程度，X 軸則是所有商品。

cues.en: You almost always see an exponential distribution like this.
cues.zh: 幾乎總會看到這種指數分布。

cues.en: Most sales come from a very small number of items, but taken together, the "long tail" makes up a large amount of sales as well.
cues.zh: 大部分銷售來自極少數項目，但整個「長尾」加總起來，也占了很大的銷售額。

cues.en: Items in that long tail, the yellow part in the graph, are items that cater to people with unique niche interests.
cues.zh: 長尾中的項目，也就是圖中黃色的部分，迎合的是具有獨特小眾興趣的人。

cues.en: Recommender systems can help people discover those items in the long tail that are relevant to their own unique niche interests.
cues.zh: 推薦系統能幫助人們，在長尾中發現符合自己獨特小眾興趣的項目。

cues.en: If you can do that successfully, then the recommendations your system makes can help new authors get discovered, can help people explore their own passions, and make money for whoever you're building
cues.zh: 如果成功，系統的推薦可以讓新作者被發現、幫助人們探索自己的熱情，也能替委託你建立

cues.en: the system for as well. Everybody wins.
cues.zh: 系統的人賺錢。所有人都受益。

cues.en: When done right, recommender systems with good novelty scores can actually make the world a better place.
cues.zh: 做得好時，具有良好新穎性分數的推薦系統，真的能讓世界更好。

cues.en: But again, you need to strike a balance between novelty and trust.
cues.zh: 但再次強調，需要在新穎性與信任之間取得平衡。

cues.en: As I said, building recommender systems is a bit of an art, and this is an example of why.
cues.zh: 就像我說的，建立推薦系統有點像藝術，這就是原因之一。
